A few questions to build a gentle daily plan for a desk-based lifestyle.
This app supports a healthy lifestyle and is not a medical device. It does not diagnose or treat. If you feel pain, dizziness or have a chronic condition, consult a doctor first.
+%1$d points. Consistency matters more than intensity.
Move and water reminders arrive hourly between 09:00 and 19:00; teeth at 08:00 and 20:00.
You have been sitting a while. Stand up and stretch for a minute.
A glass of water keeps energy and focus up.
Two minutes for a healthy smile.

1. Sit or stand tall, shoulders relaxed.
2. Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder.
3. Hold 15 seconds, breathe evenly, then switch sides.
Do not force the movement; stop if you feel sharp pain or dizziness.
1. Stand or sit tall with arms relaxed.\n2. Lift the shoulders toward the ears, then roll them back and down in a big circle.\n3. Repeat slowly, reversing direction halfway.

1. Stand in a doorway, forearms on the frame at shoulder height, elbows bent 90°.\n2. Step one foot forward until you feel a gentle stretch across the chest.\n3. Keep ribs down and neck neutral. Hold and breathe.

1. On hands and knees: wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
2. Inhale: lower the belly, lift chest and tailbone (cow).
3. Exhale: round the back, tuck chin and tailbone (cat).
4. Move slowly with your breath.

1. Kneel on one knee (use a cushion), other foot forward.\n2. Tuck the pelvis slightly and shift forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back-leg hip.\n3. Hold 20 seconds per side. Keep the torso upright.

1. Stand an arm\'s length from a wall, palms on the wall at shoulder height.\n2. Bend the elbows and bring your chest toward the wall, body in a straight line.\n3. Push back to the start with a controlled tempo.

1. Place hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line (knees down is a fine, easier version).\n2. Lower the chest toward the floor, elbows about 45° from the body.\n3. Push back up without locking the elbows hard. Breathe out on the way up.
Camera access is needed to count your reps. Video is processed on your device only: it is never saved or sent anywhere.
Place the phone about 2 m away, to your side, so your whole body is in the frame.
Counting sensitivity (if reps are missed, try Easy)
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in front of a chair.\n2. Push the hips back and lower until you lightly touch the chair, knees tracking over toes.\n3. Press through your heels to stand up.
1. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.\n2. Squeeze the glutes and lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees form a line.\n3. Pause for 1 second, then lower slowly.

1. Place forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders (knees down is fine).\n2. Keep the body in a straight line from head to heels.\n3. Brace the abs and breathe steadily. Stop if your lower back sags or hurts.
1. On hands and knees, back neutral.\n2. Extend the right arm and left leg until level with the torso.\n3. Pause, return, switch sides. Do not rotate the hips.
1. Stand holding a wall or chair for balance.\n2. Rise onto your toes as high as is comfortable.\n3. Lower slowly. Great for circulation after long sitting.
1. Walk at a pace where you can talk but not sing.\n2. Keep your head up, shoulders relaxed, arms swinging naturally.\n3. Aim for steady breathing throughout.
1. Stand tall and lift the knees alternately to hip height.\n2. Swing the arms in opposition.\n3. Keep a steady rhythm and breathe naturally.
1. Look away from the screen at something about 6 m (20 ft) away.\n2. Hold your gaze for 20 seconds and blink slowly.\n3. Repeat every 20 minutes of screen work.
